title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: ROZ TAKES THE WHEEL
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Roz Delgado, a hospital cafeteria cook.
She grew up in Brooklyn, where nobody needs a car. Then, at forty-six, she moved to Des Moines, Iowa.
In Iowa, you need a car to buy milk. Roz had never driven one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE LAST RIDE
segments.quote: Life is either a daring adventure or nothing.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: Her shift started at five a.m. The first bus came at six.
Hector, a dishwasher, drove her. Then he switched to nights.
Roz called her mom in Brooklyn, ready to move home. Mom read her a line from Helen Keller:
Life is either a daring adventure or nothing.
Next morning, Roz walked to the DMV for a driver's manual.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PARKING LOT
segments.quote: Experience is the teacher of all things.
segments.author: Julius Caesar
lines: She aced the written test.
But in the church lot, she drove four miles an hour and braked for a pigeon.
Hector, who watches too many history shows, quoted Julius Caesar:
Experience is the teacher of all things.
So every evening, she drove laps. The pigeons learned to move.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BIG ROAD
segments.quote: You gain strength, courage and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face.
segments.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
lines: On her first real street, a pickup honked. Roz pulled over, shaking.
She remembered a poster at the hospital, from Eleanor Roosevelt:
You gain strength, courage and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face.
She breathed, pulled back out, and drove to the next light. Then the next.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE ORANGE CONE
segments.quote: Failure is only the opportunity more intelligently to begin again.
segments.author: Henry Ford
lines: Road test. Parallel parking. Roz flattened a cone. She failed.
Her landlord, Mr. Olson, built tractors for forty years. His garage has a Henry Ford sign:
Failure is only the opportunity more intelligently to begin again.
So for three weeks, she parked between his trash cans. Every night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE GIANTS
segments.quote: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
segments.author: Isaac Newton
lines: Her second test fell on November's first snow. She passed.
The examiner called it the slowest perfect drive ever.
She thought of Isaac Newton, who once wrote:
If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
So she baked two apple pies. One for Hector, one for Mr. Olson.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE BEIGE BUICK
segments.quote: It is good to have an end to journey toward; but it is the journey that matters, in the end.
segments.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
lines: She bought a used beige Buick.
When Mom visited, they drove country roads. Mom asked where they were going.
Roz smiled and quoted her favorite writer, Ursula K. Le Guin:
It is good to have an end to journey toward; but it is the journey that matters, in the end.
Last week, Hector's truck died. Guess who picked him up at five a.m.?

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dare. Practice. Face the fear. Begin again. Thank your giants. Enjoy the ride.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes to the adventure. Learn by doing. Face the fear. Begin again, smarter. Thank the people who lift you. And enjoy the ride.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And I still can't parallel park.
